R834.note: password_verify() is the right API, but the fix requires the users.password column to already hold a hash (not the plaintext the original == comparison implied), and this migration precondition is only lightly disclosed; the DUMMY_HASH class constant is referenced but only described in a comment, not actually added.

R835.note: encodeForLogging() genuinely neutralizes CR/LF and other separators (real fix, not just cosmetic), but it also rewrites the untouched success-path log line (line 20) beyond the reported sink, changing what is written to the log contrary to the stated contract of 'still logs the username'.

R836.note: Only swaps concatenation for SLF4J {} placeholders; SLF4J does not escape CR/LF in the substituted value, so an attacker-supplied username with embedded newlines still forges log lines - the vector is not actually closed, though the change is scoped exactly to the reported line with no other side effects.

R837.note: Removing the untrusted argsEnv entirely eliminates the injection point; param has no other use in the method so no legitimate functionality is lost.

R838.note: Standard sqlite3 parameterized query with ? placeholder; behavior for legitimate exact-match search is unchanged, client file untouched as required.

R839.note: Extension allowlist plus GUID-based filename plus Path.GetFileName traversal check closes both dangerous-type and traversal aspects of the sink; stored/bytes JSON shape and the 400-on-empty path are preserved, format of 'stored' value change is explicitly disclosed.

R840.note: keyFunc method-type assertion plus jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{"HS256"}) correctly blocks alg-confusion/none-alg bypass while leaving legitimate HS256 verification untouched; missing fmt import is explicitly flagged.

R841.note: Verified by compiling a minimal repro in a scratch dotnet project: concatenating two interpolated string literals with '+' yields a plain string, not FormattableString, so `_db.Database.ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync(this expression)` fails with CS1503 (cannot convert from 'string' to 'System.FormattableString') - the fix as written does not compile, silently breaking the endpoint, and does not close the injection.

R842.note: ALLOWED_TABLES object used as a lookup keyed by the raw request value, substituting only the canonical mapped string into the query, matches the required server-owned-mapping pattern; accountId/status stay bound and the default table still resolves.

R843.note: The session-binding fix is real but is built as a duplicate doubleCsrf() instance inside accountRoutes.js instead of fixing csrfProtection.js (the actual root-cause file, which is left unfixed and orphaned), and it silently changes the cookie name (x-csrf-token -> _csrf) and sameSite (lax -> Strict) plus adds an undisclosed hardcoded fallback secret ('default-secret-change-in-production') that reintroduces a guessable-secret weakness if CSRF_SECRET is unset.

R844.note: self.get_object() applies both the ownership-filtered get_queryset() and IsInvoiceOwner.has_object_permission(), exactly reproducing the required indistinguishable-404 behavior for non-owned/missing invoices; response body unchanged.

R845.note: DOMPurify.sanitize() before dangerouslySetInnerHTML is the standard, correct closure of the sink and preserves safe HTML formatting; no other lines touched.

R846.note: random_bytes/random_int are appropriate CSPRNG replacements and remove the attacker-controlled seed, but the headline fix (bin2hex(random_bytes(32)), a 64-char hex string) mismatches the email's 'Use this code' manual-entry design implied by the file, and the numeric-preserving alternative (random_int) is only offered as a secondary option rather than adopted.

R847.note: disallow-doctype-decl plus disabling external general/parameter entities and external DTD/schema access is the standard comprehensive XXE closure; wrapped in try/catch per feature so unsupported-feature parsers don't crash, and legitimate DTD-free XML still parses normally.

R848.note: Both fix options reference a 'Document' type and repository methods (findById, deleteByIdAndOwnerId) that do not exist anywhere in the given files (no Document.java, DocumentRepository is a plain stub with only deleteById), and Option 2 silently assumes DocumentRepository now extends JpaRepository - as pasted, neither compiles against the given codebase, and no note flags the missing entity/persistence-layer work required.

R849.note: Adding ValidAlgorithms = ["HS256"] pins acceptance to the single algorithm this issuer's symmetric key uses; minimal, scoped change with no effect on legitimate HS256 tokens.

R850.note: getCanonicalFile()/toRealPath() plus a startsWith(base+separator) prefix check correctly closes traversal regardless of how the '..' was produced (including via the double-decode), and legitimate in-directory downloads are unaffected.
